crop.notes: Only the three-line 'Sporting Notes' item in crop-1 is about Allen (a notice for his saloon). The rest of the clipping is unrelated: the end of a contest item, 'Another Bicycle Record' (Otto Ziegler), 'Lipschutz Beat Showalter' (chess), and 'The Story of Aunt Betsy' reprinted from the New York Evening Sun, which fills crops 1–4.

ocr.notes: The Allen notice is transcribed correctly; the rest is mostly right with minor errors.

title.suggested: Notice of Free Concerts at Tom Allen's, 619 Market Street

summary.suggested: A notice under "Sporting Notes" in the St. Louis Globe-Democrat advertised Tom Allen, "retired champion pugilist of the world," at 619 Market Street, with a free concert every evening and only the best singers engaged.

metadata.notes: Masthead: St. Louis Daily Globe-Democrat, Saturday Morning, November 2, 1895, page 7.

facts.fact: In November 1895 Allen's place at 619 Market Street advertised a free concert every evening, with only the best singers engaged; he styled himself retired champion pugilist of the world

notes: Address here is 619 Market Street; the 1903 obituary (203) gives 615 Market Street. Worth checking whether the saloon moved or one figure is a misprint. Focus suggested primary because the item itself is entirely about Allen, though it is only a three-line notice; 'passing' would also be defensible.
